finding.claim: /fetch2 fetches any user-supplied URL with only a scheme check, so the attacker can reach internal hosts and metadata endpoints and read the response body.

trace.note: URL read from query string, attacker-controlled
is_http_url only checks urlparse(url).scheme in http/https
requests.get on unmodified url; redirects followed by default; first 200 bytes of body returned

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist only. No host, IP, or port validation. Redirects not disabled. Response body returned to caller.

verdict.guard_found: none. views.py:20 applies only is_http_url, which validators.py:7 implements as a scheme-only check (urlparse(url).scheme in http/https). No hostname, IP, or port validation, and views.py:22 calls requests.get(url, timeout=5) with redirects left at the requests default (followed), then returns the body text[:200]. The stricter is_safe_url at validators.py:10-18 is used only by /fetch at views.py:12, not /fetch2.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled value from views.py:19 reaches requests.get at views.py:22 after only a scheme check (validators.py:7), so internal hosts and metadata endpoints are reachable and the body is returned to the caller at views.py:22.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the destination by resolving the hostname, then fetches by hostname, so DNS rebinding can point the fetch at internal addresses.

trace.note: urlparse; scheme must be http/https and hostname present
requests.get performs lookup #2 on the same hostname independently; attacker DNS can return a public IP first and an internal IP second

finding.guards_checked: Resolved-IP blocklist (private, loopback, link-local, reserved) applied to lookup #1 only. allow_redirects=False closes redirect bypass. Scheme allowlist. Fetch not pinned to the checked IP. Response body returned to caller. Exploitability depends on attacker-controlled DNS and timing; code pattern is confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: Only validators.py:14-17, a resolved-IP blocklist (is_private/is_loopback/is_link_local/is_reserved) applied to a separate getaddrinfo lookup. This is not a closing guard under the rubric: it is not exact hostname membership, not an anchored string match, and not scheme plus host allowlist. views.py:14 calls requests.get(url) with the hostname unpinned, so it performs its own DNS lookup. allow_redirects=False (views.py:14) only blocks redirects, not rebinding. The scheme check at validators.py:12 is scheme-only.
verdict.reason: The query-string value at views.py:11 is attacker-controlled and unauthenticated, and the only gate, is_safe_url at views.py:12 / validators.py:14-17, checks IPs from one getaddrinfo call while views.py:14 re-resolves the hostname via requests.get, so DNS rebinding bypasses it and the body is returned at views.py:14. Trace minor drift: the scheme/hostname check is at validators.py:12 (not 11), and the IP-category check is at validators.py:16 (line 15 is the ip_address parse); the described logic is still accurate at those lines, so I did not mark the trace as broken.

hostname checked (no DNS check on this parse path beyond line 14)

finding.guards_checked: Hostname-derived IP blocklist (lookup on the urlparse hostname). Parser agreement between urlparse and urllib3 not confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: validators.py:14-17 resolves parsed.hostname via socket.getaddrinfo and rejects private, loopback, link-local, and reserved addresses, and views.py:12-13 returns 400 when is_safe_url is False. This is a DNS and IP-range check, not an exact hostname match. The trace's note that there is "no DNS check beyond line 14" is wrong, because line 14 is the DNS check.
verdict.reason: The trace misdescribes validators.py:12-17 (the DNS and private-IP guard starts at line 14, not after it), and the claimed differential is unsupported: urlparse at validators.py:11 and urllib3's authority split both take the host after the last '@' with backslash not treated as a delimiter, so both would yield example.com, and the candidate cites no urllib3 behavior showing otherwise. The /fetch2 route (views.py:19-22) is a separate scheme-only issue that this candidate does not describe.
